sentences.text: CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE M.NAGAPRASANNA
ORAL ORDER

The petitioners - husband and his family members are before this Court calling in question registration of a crime in Crime No.91/2024, pending before the 11th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Mayo Hall, Bengaluru, for the offences under Sections 498A, 506, 504 and 34 of the IPC along with Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

entities.text: 11th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Mayo Hall, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 would submit that respondent No.2 is represented through special power of attorney holder as she is working abroad.
The special power of attorney is submitted before the Court.

3. Learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2, in unison would submit that during the pendency of this petition, the parties to the lis have arrived at settlement by drawing up certain terms and conditions and decided to obtain a decree of divorce on mutual consent.
A joint application NC: 2024:KHC:51056 under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C. is also filed before this Court to that effect.

4. The joint application reads as follows:
".... .... ....
3.
The well-wishers of the both the families and their respective Counsel have advised the petitioners and the 2nd Respondent and her parents to amicably resolve the dispute in their best interest.
The Petitioners and the 2nd Respondent, having realized the reality of life and keeping in mind the paramount interests of their respective lives, have mutually agreed to the suggestion.
That in furtherance of the have filed a Petition under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act 1956 seeking for dissolution of their marriage by way of mutual consent.
4. The Respondent No.2 hereby withdraws all allegations against the Petitioners herein.

The Respondent No. 2 wife herein does not intend to pursue and prosecute the Criminal Case filed by her in Crime No. 0006/2024, pending on the file of the Hon'ble Court of 24th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Bengaluru City and has got no objection to allow the above Criminal Petition No. 9361/2024 to quash the aforesaid criminal proceedings in Crime No. 0006/2024.
5.

entities.text: 24th Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate at Bengaluru City
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Petitioners and the 2nd Respondent do hereby state that they have filed the above application on their own free will and volition, there is no coercion or fraud."

In the light of the fact that the parties have arrived at settlement and decided to part their ways and as the dispute revolves around the husband and the wife, I deem it appropriate to accept the joint application and terminate the proceedings against the petitioners, as the allegations are not against the State.
